/-!
# Sections to divisors — the DAT-A2 germ-regularity bridge

The geometry layer of the `lm:ctn` (iii)⟹(i) slicing criterion
(`informal/spec-dat-a.md` §2; core: `AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.FibrewiseRegular`):

* **(α) germ transport** — `IsAffineOpen.germ_mem_nonZeroDivisors`: a nonzerodivisor of
  the section ring of an affine open has nonzerodivisor germs at all of its points
  (stalks are localizations of the affine section ring; regularity passes to
  localizations). This is also the "germ-level regularity by localization-exactness"
  consumption surface of DD-1a (dat-d-worksheet §1.2).
* **(the field-level slice case, Kleiman tex 2013–2022)** —
  `Scheme.germ_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_ne_zero`: on an **integral** scheme a nonzero
  section has nonzerodivisor germs everywhere on its open. This is the named lemma
  DAT-C discharges at field-level fibres ("nonzero on the integral fibre ⟹ regular").
* **(β) piece flatness** — `flat_sections_basicOpen`: over `Spec k`, if the affine
  chart ring is `k`-flat (`Scheme.overModule`) then so is every basic-open piece ring
  (tower `k → Γ(V) → Γ(D(h))` through `IsAffineOpen.isLocalization_basicOpen`).
* **(γ) the generic A2 bridge** — `mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_fibrewise_regular` (+ germ
  form): over a Noetherian `k`, a section of a basic-open piece of a `k`-flat affine
  chart that is **fibrewise regular** (multiplication injective on every residue-field
  fibre of the piece ring, in `Scheme.mulSectionEnd`/`rTensor` form) is a nonzerodivisor
  with nonzerodivisor germs. The tensor-RING form of the fibre hypothesis converts
  through `injective_rTensor_mulSectionEnd_of_tmul_mem_nonZeroDivisors`.
* **(δ) A2 on the pinned datum** — for `D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π` and a global
  section `s` of the DAT-1 glued sheaf, each component `D.component s j` (the section on
  the trivializing basic-open piece `D(h_j)`) is a nonzerodivisor with nonzerodivisor
  germs, given its fibrewise regularity (`component_mem_nonZeroDivisors`,
  `germ_component_mem_nonZeroDivisors`). These are exactly the `regular` inputs of
  `Scheme.LocalEquations` — the LocalEquations construction and the class law are in
  `AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.SectionsToDivisorsClass`.

The fibrewise hypothesis is deliberately the *piece-ring residue-fibre* spelling
(worksheet §2.2.2 with §5 risk 4 discharged): it is vacuous on pieces missing a fibre
(zero ring), it is exactly what the integral-fibre slice case produces where the fibre
ring is a domain, and it keeps the un-landed 1d-ii/DAT-3 fibre-sheaf identifications
with their owners (DAT-C/DD-R bridge their fibre-curve statements to this spelling).
-/

divisor identities used by the basepoint-free pencil trick at every translate
`A = B + S`. -/
theorem divisor_pencil_lattice_of_basepointFree
    (A B S : X.CurveDivisor) (v0 v1 : X.functionFieldˣ)
    (hA : A = B + S)
    (hbpf : (S + Scheme.divOf (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) v0) ⊓
        (S + Scheme.divOf (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) v1) = 0) :
    ((B - Scheme.divOf (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) v0) ⊔
        (B - Scheme.divOf (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) v1) = A) ∧
      ((A + Scheme.divOf (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) v0) ⊓
        (A + Scheme.divOf (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) v1) = B) := by
  let D0 := Scheme.divOf (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) v0
  let D1 := Scheme.divOf (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) v1
  have hbpf' : (S + D0) ⊓ (S + D1) = 0 := hbpf
  constructor

      (B - D0) ⊔ (B - D1) =
          (A - (S + D0)) ⊔ (A - (S + D1)) := by
            rw [hA]
            congr 1 <;> abel
      _ = A - ((S + D0) ⊓ (S + D1)) :=

lemma thetaFieldPresentation_cocycle :
    (thetaFieldPresentation C K π a).cocycle = thetaFieldCocycle C K π a :=
  rfl

variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (relCurve C K ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
  [QuasiCompact (relCurve C K ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]

/-- **The theta divisor at the field test** `N₀(a)`: the presentation divisor of the
theta presentation — an honest Weil divisor on the fibre curve in the `K`-level theta
class `Θᵃ`. -/
noncomputable def thetaFieldDivisor : (relCurve C K).CurveDivisor :=
  Scheme.presentationDivisor K (thetaFieldPresentation C K π a)

/-- The theta divisor lies in the class of the `K`-level whole-chart theta datum. -/
theorem picClass_thetaFieldDivisor :
    Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass K (thetaFieldDivisor C K π a)
      = (thetaChartDatum C K π a).cechPicClass := by
  rw [thetaFieldDivisor, Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass_presentationDivisor]
  exact (thetaChartDatum C K π a).cechPicClass_eq_mk (thetaFieldPointedCover C K π)
    (thetaFieldChartIndex C K π) (fun _ => le_rfl)

/-- **The transported window divisor and the theta divisor share their class** (the
base-change seam, closed by `cechPicClass_baseChange_thetaChartDatum`): the abstract `N`
of the DDR-2 `N`-pack and the concrete `N₀(a)` of the reading are linearly
equivalent. -/
theorem picClass_windowTransportDivisor_eq_thetaFieldDivisor :
    Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass K (windowTransportDivisor C K π a)
      = Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass K (thetaFieldDivisor C K π a) := by
  rw [picClass_windowTransportDivisor, picClass_thetaFieldDivisor]
  exact cechPicClass_baseChange_thetaChartDatum C K π a

variable [LocallyOfFiniteType (relCurve C K ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]

/-- **The shift unit**: a rational function with
`div w = thetaFieldDivisor − windowTransportDivisor`, extracted from the class equality
(extraction (X), `exists_divOf_of_picClass_eq`).  Multiplication by `w` transports the
reading from the concrete `N₀(a)` to the abstract transported window divisor. -/
noncomputable def thetaFieldShiftUnit : (relCurve C K).functionFieldˣ :=
  (Scheme.CurveDivisor.exists_divOf_of_picClass_eq K
    (picClass_windowTransportDivisor_eq_thetaFieldDivisor C K π a).symm).choose

lemma divOf_thetaFieldShiftUnit :
    thetaFieldDivisor C K π a - windowTransportDivisor C K π a
      = Scheme.divOf (relCurve C K ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))
          (thetaFieldShiftUnit C K π a) :=
  (Scheme.CurveDivisor.exists_divOf_of_picClass_eq K
    (picClass_windowTransportDivisor_eq_thetaFieldDivisor C K π a).symm).choose_spec

## STEP A — producing two distinct effective divisors from `2 ≤ h⁰`: **ABSENT**

Nothing in AJCR produces a pair of distinct divisors, and there is **no map from H⁰ sections to effective divisors as a function**. What exists is the one-shot existential.

**The keystone (uniqueness direction only)** — `/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/RiemannRoch/EffectiveUniqueness.lean:144`:

```lean
variable (K : Type u) [Field K] {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))] [IsIntegral X]
  -- plus (from line 77): [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
  --                      [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
theorem CurveDivisor.eq_of_picClass_eq_of_h0_one {D D' : X.CurveDivisor}
    (hD : 0 ≤ D) (hD' : 0 ≤ D')
    (hcl : CurveDivisor.picClass K D = CurveDivisor.picClass K D')
    (hone : Sheaf.h0 (X.divisorSheaf K D) = 1) :
    D' = D
```
Note this is stated on an abstract `X`, not on `relCurve C K`; the worker form with the `finrank` hypothesis is at line 110 (`eq_of_picClass_eq_of_finrank_one`). Instance binders include `LocallyOfFiniteType` and `QuasiCompact` (declared at line 77-78, so both theorems carry them).

**The section-to-divisor step, existential only** — `RiemannRoch/SectionBound.lean:175`:

```lean
variable (K : Type u) [Field K] {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))] [IsIntegral X]
  [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
  -- the two Module.Finite binders are `omit`ted for this theorem (lines 167-168)
theorem exists_effective_of_h0_pos (A : X.CurveDivisor)
    (hA : 0 < Sheaf.h0 (X.divisorSheaf K A)) :
    ∃ E : X.CurveDivisor, 0 ≤ E ∧ CurveDivisor.picClass K E = CurveDivisor.picClass K A
```
Its proof picks **one** arbitrary nonzero section via `exists_ne (0 : Sheaf.HModule …)` and returns `A + divOf u`. It is not a function of the section, so you cannot feed it two independent sections and compare outputs. Sibling: `exists_effective_of_picClass` (`RiemannRoch/FLVClass.lean:208`), same shape with the Riemann-inequality entry `1 ≤ deg W + χ`.

**Searched and absent** (patterns, all repo-wide over `AlgebraicJacobian/**/*.lean`, case-insensitive where noted): `divisorOfSection`, `sectionDivisor`, `divOfSection`, `divisorOf`, `effectiveDivisorOf`, `divZeros`, `zerosDivisor` — zero hits. `ofSection` — only `Scheme.QcohOn.ofSectionsEquiv` (a sheaf-sections equivalence, unrelated). `zeroDivisor` — only `nonZeroDivisors`. `toDivisor` — only presheaf-map names (`gluedToDivisorApp`, `moduleToDivisorZeroPresheaf`, …) plus `SectionsToDivisors`, which is the *relative* germ-regularity bridge, not a linear-system map (see below).

**No `h0 = 1 ↔ uniqueness`, no contrapositive `1 < h0 → ∃ D₁ ≠ D₂`.** I ran an AST-ish scan over every declaration in the project extracting the statement (text before `:=`/`by`) and selecting those containing both `∃` and `≠` together with `CurveDivisor` or `DivFam`: 28 declarations, none of which has a divisor-inequality in its conclusion (they are `≠ 0`, `≠ genericPoint`, `x ≠ y` in achiever/base-divisor lemmas). A single-line grep for `∃.*≠` excluding `≠ 0`/`genericPoint`/`≠ ⊤`/`≠ ⊥` yields exactly one hit project-wide, in `Curve/SeparablyClosedFibre.lean:111` (about polynomial evaluation). `2 ≤ Sheaf.h0` occurs in **hypothesis position nowhere** — its only four occurrences are the two conclusions in `Pic0ChartLocusH0Rank.lean:125,234`. `h0_eq_one_iff` does not exist.

**What is landed instead, and it runs the wrong way.** `Picard/Pic0ChartLocusH0One.lean` builds the whole `h⁰ = 1` route: `h0_eq_one_of_subsingleton_of_deg` (line 102), `eq_of_picClass_eq_of_deg_of_subsingleton` (line 169, discharges `hone` from `deg W = n` + `Subsingleton H¹` + `χ = 1 - n`), `exists_effective_picClass_eq_of_h0_eq_one` (line 188), and the payoff `existsUnique_effective_of_mem_chartLocus` (line 201), whose conclusion is `0 ≤ E ∧ ∀ E', 0 ≤ E' → picClass L E' = M → E' = E`. **The nearest thing to two divisors in one class** is the pencil: `Picard/DivSchemeHighWindowPencilTheta.lean:321` `thetaFieldPencil_basepointFree` gives two units `thetaFieldPencilFstUnit`/`thetaFieldPencilSndUnit` with `(N₀ + div v₀) ⊓ (N₀ + div v₁) = 0` — two effective divisors in the class of `thetaFieldDivisor`, with disjoint support. The base-divisor machinery (`RiemannRoch/BaseDivisor.lean`, `BaseDivisorSpan.lean`) computes pointwise minima over a whole subspace and has the `divOf_smul` scalar-invariance (line 118) — but not the converse (`div f = div g → ∃ c, f = c • g`), which is what a distinctness argument needs.
